newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt wins second confidence vote in a week.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt wins second confidence vote in a week.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government on Friday won its second vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament this week as it battled to meet tight new deadlines for the ratification of cabinet decree laws.
Friday's do-or-die vote covered legislation for the reorganisation of the transport sector which has to be converted into law by next Wednesday or else discarded.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition, which depends on the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for its majority in the lower house, won the motion by 308 to 170.

The government has resorted to numerous confidence votes during its 10 months in office after a court decision banning the cabinet from the traditional practice of re-issuing old decrees. Under the new system, a cabinet bill automatically expires after 60 days unless passed into law by parliament.

The court ruling has given the government a legislative nightmare, making it virtually impossible to push decrees onto the statute books without recourse to a confidence vote, unless it gets the go-ahead from the opposition.
Earlier this week, Prodi called a confidence vote to brush aside hundreds of opposition amendments to the final part of the 1997 austerity budget.
Friday's vote was on an umbrella amendment covering articles of a transport decree, which will reform the fiscal system for the sector and cut the number of motorway tariffs for haulage companies.
The centre-right opposition bloc headed by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi has condemned the regular use of confidence votes, saying it runs against the spirit of democracy.

"(The government) is trying to limit the ability of the opposition to propose amendments," Italo Bocchino, a member of parliament for the hard-right National Alliance party, said during the debate on the transport confidence motion.
